**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Pure Mathematics with Mechanics, Paper 3 (0765/3), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2022. Time allowed: three hours.**

Full marks may be obtained for answers to ALL questions. All questions carry equal marks. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. Mathematical formulae booklet published by the GCE Board are allowed. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving the answer at each stage. Calculators are allowed. Start each question on a fresh page.
incertitudes: Le sujet n'imprime pas de total de points par question ; l'énoncé dit seulement « All questions carry equal marks ». Les points imprimés par partie somment à 13 pour chacune des 8 questions (total 104) ; `points` de l'exercice est laissé vide.

Question 2 (i) : le sujet dit « smooth plane » ET donne un coefficient de frottement 2/5 entre P et le plan : énoncé contradictoire. L'énoncé de (a) est recopié tel qu'imprimé (« smooth » conservé). Le corrigé retient le plan RUGUEUX avec mu = 2/5 (donnée explicite, qui produit des valeurs propres : T = 100 + 40 sqrt3 / 3, force sur la poulie 100 sqrt3 + 40) et donne à la fin de chaque partie la valeur pour le plan lisse (a = 5, T = 100 N, 100 sqrt3 N). Les parties (b) et (c) du sujet n'impriment pas de rappel du contexte : il est recopié dans l'énoncé de chaque sous-question pour qu'elle soit autonome.

Question 2 (ii) : le sujet dit seulement « an acceleration of 8 pi^2 / 81 » ; le corrigé la lit comme l'accélération centripète d'un mouvement circulaire uniforme (hypothèse signalée entre crochets dans le corrigé). Le sujet imprime « Take g as 10 m s^-2 » après la question 2 : valeur retenue g = 10 (utilisée en (i)).

questions.enonce_markdown:
A body $P$ of mass $10\ \mathrm{kg}$, lying on a smooth plane inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal, is connected to another body $Q$, of mass $20\ \mathrm{kg}$, by a light inextensible string which passes over a fixed smooth pulley at the top of the plane. The system is released from rest when $Q$ is hanging vertically. Given that the coefficient of friction between $P$ and the plane is $\dfrac25$, find

the acceleration of $P$,

(Take $g$ as $10\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$.)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Reading of the problem.** The statement calls the plane "smooth" but also gives a coefficient of friction $\mu = \tfrac25$ between $P$ and the plane. These two statements contradict each other; since the value $\mu = \tfrac25$ is given as data ("Given that..."), the plane is taken as **rough with $\mu = \tfrac25$**. (The smooth case, $\mu = 0$, is given at the end of this part.) $g = 10\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$ as printed.

**Diagram described.** $P$ is on the plane (angle $30^\circ$); the string runs from $P$ up the plane, over the pulley at the top, and down vertically to $Q$. Forces on $P$: weight $10g = 100\ \mathrm{N}$ vertically down, normal reaction $R$ perpendicular to the plane, tension $T$ up the plane, friction $F$ down the plane (opposing the motion). Forces on $Q$: weight $20g = 200\ \mathrm{N}$ down, tension $T$ up. The inextensible string gives both bodies the same acceleration $a$. **Positive direction:** up the plane for $P$, downwards for $Q$ (the direction of motion).

**Does the system move?** The driving force $200\ \mathrm{N}$ exceeds $100\sin 30^\circ + \mu R = 50 + 20\sqrt3 \approx 84.6\ \mathrm{N}$, so $Q$ descends and $P$ moves up the plane; friction on $P$ is therefore limiting and acts down the plane.

**Perpendicular to the plane (for $P$):**

$$R = 100\cos 30^\circ = 50\sqrt3\ \mathrm{N},\qquad F = \mu R = \tfrac25\times 50\sqrt3 = 20\sqrt3\ \mathrm{N}\approx 34.6\ \mathrm{N}$$

**Equations of motion ($F = ma$):**

$$P:\quad T - 100\sin 30^\circ - 20\sqrt3 = 10a \;\Longrightarrow\; T - 50 - 20\sqrt3 = 10a$$

$$Q:\quad 200 - T = 20a$$

Adding eliminates $T$:

$$150 - 20\sqrt3 = 30a \;\Longrightarrow\; a = 5 - \frac{2\sqrt3}{3}\approx 3.85\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$$

**Acceleration of $P$: $a = 5 - \dfrac{2\sqrt3}{3} \approx 3.85\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$ up the plane.**

(If the plane were truly smooth, $\mu = 0$: $150 = 30a$ gives $a = 5\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$, $T = 100\ \mathrm{N}$ and a force on the pulley of $100\sqrt3 \approx 173\ \mathrm{N}$.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
With the data of part (i)(a) ($P$ of mass $10\ \mathrm{kg}$ on a plane inclined at $30^\circ$, coefficient of friction $\dfrac25$, connected over a smooth pulley to $Q$ of mass $20\ \mathrm{kg}$ hanging vertically, released from rest, $g = 10\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$), find

the tension in the string,
questions.corrige_markdown:
From the equation for $Q$ (positive downwards): $200 - T = 20a$, with $a = 5 - \dfrac{2\sqrt3}{3}$:

$$T = 200 - 20\left(5 - \frac{2\sqrt3}{3}\right) = 100 + \frac{40\sqrt3}{3}\approx 123\ \mathrm{N}$$

**Check with $P$:** $T = 50 + 20\sqrt3 + 10a = 50 + 34.64 + 38.45 = 123.09\ \mathrm{N}$. Consistent.

**Tension $T = 100 + \dfrac{40\sqrt3}{3} \approx 123\ \mathrm{N}$.** (Smooth plane: $T = 100\ \mathrm{N}$.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
With the same data as in part (i)(a), find

the magnitude of the force exerted by the string on the pulley.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The string passes over the smooth pulley, so the tension is $T$ in both parts. One part of the string runs from the pulley **down the plane** to $P$, that is at $30^\circ$ below the horizontal; the other part hangs **vertically down** to $Q$. Each part pulls the pulley with a force $T$ along the string, away from the pulley. The angle between the two parts of the string is $90^\circ - 30^\circ = 60^\circ$.

Resolving the two pulls (horizontal axis towards the plane, vertical axis upwards):

$$\text{horizontal: } T\cos 30^\circ,\qquad \text{vertical: } -T\sin 30^\circ - T = -\tfrac32 T$$

$$|\mathbf{F}_{\text{pulley}}| = T\sqrt{\cos^2 30^\circ + \tfrac94} = T\sqrt{\tfrac34 + \tfrac94} = \sqrt3\,T$$

(Equivalently $2T\cos\tfrac{60^\circ}{2} = 2T\cos 30^\circ = \sqrt3\,T$.) With $T = 100 + \dfrac{40\sqrt3}{3}$:

$$|\mathbf{F}_{\text{pulley}}| = 100\sqrt3 + 40\approx 213\ \mathrm{N}$$

The force acts along the bisector of the two parts of the string, i.e. at $30^\circ$ to the downward vertical, directed downwards and towards the plane.

**Force on the pulley $= 100\sqrt3 + 40 \approx 213\ \mathrm{N}$.** (Smooth plane: $100\sqrt3 \approx 173\ \mathrm{N}$.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
A particle moves in a circle of radius $2\ \mathrm{m}$ with an acceleration of $\dfrac{8\pi^2}{81}\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$.

Find its angular displacement in $3\ \mathrm{s}$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Model.** A particle that moves in a circle with a single given acceleration is taken to be in uniform circular motion (constant speed); its acceleration is then purely centripetal, of magnitude $a = \omega^2 r$, where $\omega$ is the constant angular speed. [This reading is an assumption: the question does not say that the speed is constant.]

$$\omega^2 = \frac{a}{r} = \frac{8\pi^2/81}{2} = \frac{4\pi^2}{81}\;\Longrightarrow\;\omega = \frac{2\pi}{9}\ \mathrm{rad\,s^{-1}}$$

(Check: $v = \omega r = \dfrac{4\pi}{9}$ and $v^2/r = \dfrac{16\pi^2/81}{2} = \dfrac{8\pi^2}{81}$.)

Angular displacement in $t = 3\ \mathrm{s}$:

$$\theta = \omega t = \frac{2\pi}{9}\times 3 = \frac{2\pi}{3}\ \mathrm{rad}$$

**Angular displacement $= \dfrac{2\pi}{3}\ \mathrm{rad}$ ($= 120^\circ$, one third of a revolution).**
